hero.label: Made for Sirdab
hero.headline: I want to help Sirdab own the MENA warehousing market.
hero.subheadline: Sirdab is solving a genuinely broken problem: businesses across Saudi Arabia have been stuck with rigid, slow, commitment-heavy warehouse contracts for too long. The on-demand model you have built is the kind of infrastructure shift that only happens once in a market, and I want to be part of the team closing the deals that prove it. From cold outreach at Copygen.ai to B2B growth work at NextAfter, I have spent the last two years doing exactly this kind of pipeline-building work.

whyCompany.title: Sirdab is solving real friction, not a manufactured problem
whyCompany.body: Naif and Abdulrahman built Sirdab because they watched businesses lose time and money to inflexible warehouse commitments firsthand. That origin matters: the product exists because the pain was real, not because a slide deck said the market was big. Selling a solution rooted in genuine operational frustration is a completely different conversation than selling a feature.

whyCompany.title: YC W23 with serious hiring momentum across seven roles
whyCompany.body: Sirdab is at the exact stage where a great BDR can shape how the sales motion gets built, not just execute someone else's playbook. Seven open roles across engineering, design, marketing, and sales signals that the team is scaling with intention right now. Joining here means the deals I close and the outreach sequences I build will actually influence how the company grows.

whyCompany.title: I have done this exact job, just in a different vertical
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach from scratch using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and helped bring in 15 to 20 paying clients. At NextAfter I worked inside a B2B consultancy learning how to build trust with business buyers through content and targeted campaigns. The workflow of finding the right contact, earning a conversation, and moving a deal forward is something I have been doing for over a year.

quote: Cloud warehousing in MENA is one of those rare moments where the infrastructure of an entire region is being rebuilt from scratch. I want to be the person knocking on doors and making that story land.
